why: I checked all 11 expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked at the PR head before merge. Nine use `run` proofs: local commands such as `npm ci`, `npx --no-install jsonl-lint` on temp files made with `printf`, `grep` counts and exit codes, all with exact expected values (e.g. "expect exit=1 and exactly the two lines `/tmp/bad.jsonl:2:` and `/tmp/bad.jsonl:4:`"). The test-suite line also asks for "the CI `test` check on the PR", and that check runs on the PR before merge. Two lines use `read` proofs on package.json and README.md "at the PR head", with concrete things to look for (no `dependencies`, `"type": "module"`, the 'No tools yet' bullet gone). Nothing depends on publishing, a release, a deploy or a live page; publishing to npm is listed as a non-goal. The weakest line is "a usage message", which still has a clear check: exit 2 and stderr that isn't empty.
